title: Introduce Economic Stitcher: tenant-aware batch stitching and quantization-fallback guardian
author: Priya Nair
description:
Motivation: tenant traffic shapes are increasingly multimodal (short chat, mid-form assistants, large doc summarization). Our current batching defaults and quantization tiers are optimized for a single dominant shape per tenant which leads to suboptimal unit economics when traffic mixes. This PR introduces the 'Economic Stitcher' — a light-weight tenant-aware batch stitching layer that: 1) observes recent sequence-length histograms, 2) generates per-tenant stitching templates (micro-batches that preserve latency SLOs while increasing GPU packing), and 3) provides a safe quantization-fallback guardian that dynamically routes to a compatible quantized model variant when cost/burst thresholds are hit.

This description is intentionally a single continuous string. Changes in this PR: - Add a tenant stitcher service that computes stitching templates and exposes them via the config-service cache. - Add a quant-fallback guardian that exports simple cost signals (expected tokens/sec, tail-latency impact) and a ranked list of compatible quant profiles. - Integrate stitcher outputs into the serving runtime's batch planner (heuristic hook). - CLI tool (econctl) additions: dry-run, simulate, and export templates for auditing. - Unit economics telemetry: new metrics and dashboard tags to measure per-tenant unit cost before/after stitch. Checklist: - [x] Design doc (linked in ENG-1987) - [x] Unit tests for stitcher templates and guardian rules - [x] Integration test with batch planner simulation harness - [x] Telemetry emitted and dashboard prototype - [x] Migration/runtime fallback with zero-downtime config publish Implementation notes: - The stitcher runs as a periodic job (default 5m cadence) and keeps a short-lived working set per tenant (max 1k tenants in memory). Templates are tiny (3–6 integers) and stored in the config cache with TTLs. - The guardian evaluates a cost delta heuristic and exposes an allowlist of quant profiles per model family; changes are conservative by default and require manual opt-in for any aggressive quant profile. - The runtime hook is opt-in via a feature flag 'runtime.econ_stitcher.enabled' scoped to tenant and cluster. - No model file changes; quant profiles reference existing artifacts and are validated against the model-registry during deploy. Commits summary: - initial: introduce stitcher core and template format - add: guardian cost heuristics and profile ranking - add: econctl CLI simulate/dry-run commands and output formatter - integrate: runtime batch-planner hook and feature gating - tests: unit + integration harness + telemetry mocks Changed files (high level): - services/econ-stitcher/core.py: template generator and validation logic - services/econ-stitcher/guardian.py: cost heuristics and profile ranking - infra/config-cache/requests.go: small API to fetch stitch templates - runtime/batch_planner/heuristics.go: opt-in hook to consume stitch templates - tools/econctl/cli.py: simulate/dry-run/export commands - telemetry/metrics_defs.yaml: new telemetry keys and labels - docs/ops/econ-stitcher.md: rollout, runbook, and auditing instructions - tests/integration/econ_stitcher_sim_test.py: harness changes Small illustrative snippets (for reviewers): - template format: {tenant_id: "t-123", templates: [[4,8],[1,1,6]], ttl_s: 300} - guardian rule (pseudocode): if projected_unit_cost > threshold and tail_p50_latency < slo_margin then consider_quant_fallback() Testing & results: - Synthetic mixed workload (60% short, 30% medium, 10% long) in the integration harness showed a median unit-cost reduction of 12% and a 95th percentile latency change within ±3% under default conservative profiles. - We also ran a conservative tenant-bounded canary (500 tenants) in prod-preview for 48h: no SLO regressions observed, telemetry matched simulation within noise bounds. Rollout plan: - Feature gated behind runtime.econ_stitcher.enabled - Phase 1 (dry-run): 2 weeks - Phase 2 (canary): 1% tenants 48h - Phase 3 (ramped): 10% -> 50% -> 100% over 2 weeks with safe rollback. Backout: revert feature flag. Security and compliance: no PII changes, templates stored encrypted at rest via existing config cache KMS. Operational impact: new telemetry adds additional cardinality tags (tenant_id) but those are sampled and only emitted when stitcher enabled for the tenant. Backwards compatibility: stitcher is opt-in; runtime respects absent template keys and falls back to current batching policy. Related work: extends ideas from ENG-2024 (batcher heuristics) and reuses quant-profile validation code from the model-registry. Merge notes: squash merge after CI green and approvals. Release notes: added below.

review_thread: Ethan Brooks: Nice shape. Two asks: (1) add a small microbenchmark showing stitching CPU overhead, (2) ensure we have a conservative limit on auto-applied quant profiles.
Priya Nair: Added CPU microbenchmark (bench/stitch_bench.go) and a hard cap of 2 auto-applied quant profiles per tenant. Updated tests to cover cap. PTAL.

Priya Nair: Switched to 10m default cadence and added a tenant-level override. Also added sampling to telemetry emission to keep cardinality in bounds.
Carlos Vega: Approved — telemetry looks sane and the integration tests cover the main flows. Recommend squash+merge after CI passes.

release_notes: Adds 'Economic Stitcher' (tenant-aware batch templates) and a conservative quantization-fallback guardian. Feature is opt-in behind runtime.econ_stitcher.enabled. Provides econctl CLI for dry-run/simulate/export, new telemetry keys for per-tenant unit cost comparison, and docs with rollout/runbook. Default behavior is conservative; no automatic aggressive quantization without manual opt-in.
notes_for_ops: Operators: watch telemetry.metric.econ.unit_cost.delta and runtime.econ_stitcher.applied_templates.count. If you see sustained >10% unit cost regressions or >5% tail latency increase, flip runtime.econ_stitcher.enabled=false for affected tenants and open ENG-1987. For high-cardinality clusters, ensure config-cache nodes are scaled before enabling widespread rollout.
audit_trail: config-cache writes are logged to existing audit stream. Stitch templates include opaque verification hashes and guardian decisions emit decision_id for traceability.
